rules.sentence: A patent foramen ovale connects the right and left atria and is usually found as an incidental finding on an echocardiogram or after a cryptogenic stroke.
The thrombus could travel from the left atrium into the systemic circulation, where it can, unfortunately, be delivered to the brain, causing a thromboembolic cerebrovascular accident (CVA).
The most worrisome complication of pulmonary circulation dysfunction is a pulmonary embolism, which usually arises as a deep venous thrombosis (DVT) of the lower extremity.
Rarely do DVTs occur without satisfying at least one of the three components of Virchow’s triad: hypercoagulability, endothelial damage, and venous stasis.
If the deep venous thrombus is dislodged from the lower extremity, it is pushed by deoxygenated blood back into the heart and then into the lungs, where it can lodge into a small pulmonary vessel.
